sources: empirical run of v1.0.1 release binary on this machine

findings.title: Windows installer silently wipes HKCU\Environment\Path when value name is not exactly 'Path'
findings.impact: Data loss: existing user PATH entries are replaced by a single-entry value; rollback then *deletes* the value entirely instead of restoring it.
findings.evidence: windows_path.rs:69-88 (case-sensitive strip_prefix('Path')); install/lib.rs:518-583 (apply blindly uses None); install/lib.rs:628-637 (rollback enters delete branch because existed:false was persisted in the manifest).
findings.repro: On a machine where HKCU\Environment\Path was previously written by `setx PATH ...` from CMD (stored as PATH or path), run `tokenzero install --apply` then `tokenzero install --rollback latest`. User PATH is empty.
findings.fix: Match the value name case-insensitively; treat parse-miss with exit-0 as fatal abort; in rollback() re-check live registry state before deleting when entry.existed is false.

findings.title: tz:// refs use only 64 bits of SHA-256 and overwrite on collision
findings.impact: `expand` can silently return wrong bytes for a valid ref, breaking the core 'byte-exact recoverable' invariant.
findings.evidence: core/lib.rs:1528-1536 truncates SHA-256 to 8 bytes; recovery/lib.rs:559-562 inserts by id with no length/hash verification.
findings.fix: Store full SHA-256 hash + length alongside the ref id; verify on expand; collision bucket or refuse to serve on detected collision.
findings.claim_contradicted: docs/racc.md:45 'dangling refs never return wrong bytes'

findings.title: Refs can be evicted before the response that advertises them returns
findings.impact: A single large payload or cache-pressure event can hand the agent a `tz://` it cannot expand. Capsule-level liveness check happens before the persist, eviction happens after.
findings.evidence: mcp/lib.rs:355-356, :446-490 (refs pushed before persist_pending, no re-check); recovery/lib.rs:681-779 (evict runs before write, drops oldest live refs while over max_bytes).
findings.fix: Pin the current response's refs through persist, or re-verify with has_ref after eviction; if they can't fit, return degraded output with no refs or atomically expand capacity for the current call.
findings.claim_contradicted: README 'byte-exact recoverable'; docs/racc.md:55 'exact refs with no dangling handles'

findings.title: MCP traffic is not Pulse-accounted; 'savings after recovery' is untrue on the main integration surface
findings.impact: `tz_expand` calls over MCP never charge recovery tokens back to the original serve, so the headline RACC accounting claim does not hold for agent-routed usage (the only real-world surface).
findings.evidence: mcp/tools.rs:14-21 (MCP dispatch returns response with no Pulse write); CLI commands DO call record_tool_pulse at tokenzero/src/main.rs:448, :719; pulse events lack session/call ids (pulse/src/lib.rs:19-35; docs/pulse.md:220-223).
findings.fix: Instrument Pulse at the MCP tools/call boundary (including tz_expand); include stable session/call/ref ids so recovery can be attributed back to the original serve.
findings.claim_contradicted: README 'Savings are counted after any recovery'

findings.title: `tz_fetch` is an unrestricted SSRF / exfiltration primitive
findings.impact: Any MCP-capable agent can fetch arbitrary http(s) URLs (loopback, link-local, cloud metadata endpoints, internal services) and cache the bodies behind refs.
findings.evidence: mcp/tools.rs:201-209 (fetch exposed unconditionally); mcp/lib.rs:1674-1718 (only checks http(s) prefix, then invokes `curl -sS -L`).
findings.fix: Default to network-off; add allow/deny lists; block loopback, RFC1918, link-local, and metadata IPs after DNS resolution; cap redirects; log fetches as security-relevant telemetry.

findings.title: Supervisor can send both a retryable error and a real response for the same JSON-RPC id
findings.impact: Strict MCP clients may treat duplicate replies as protocol violations and tear down the session; resent reply also hardcodes framed=false.
findings.evidence: mcp/supervisor.rs:157-166 (tracks request, stores as pending_resend on failed write), :424-438 (drains all outstanding ids with retryable errors), :451-453 + :475-484 (resend with framed=false).
findings.fix: For a message known not to reach the child, remove its id from outstanding before emitting retryable errors; preserve original framing on resend; return either an error or a replay, never both.

findings.title: `collect_search` / `collect_glob` recurse forever on symlink loops inside an allowed root
findings.impact: Single `tz_find` or `tz_glob` against a tree with a symlink cycle → stack overflow / wall-clock DoS. `collect_tree` is depth-bounded; these two aren't, which makes the asymmetry hard to spot in review.
findings.evidence: mcp/collect.rs:177-251 (collect_search), :493-534 (collect_glob); both call path.is_dir() which follows links; no visited-set, no depth bound. max_files only stops when results vector is full.
findings.fix: Mirror collect_tree's depth bound; skip entries where file_type.is_symlink(); or switch to walkdir::WalkDir::new().follow_links(false).max_depth(N).

findings.title: `record_fetch` corrupts/loses the fetch index under any concurrency or crash
findings.impact: Two concurrent tz_fetch calls (4-worker MCP pool or two processes against the same cache) silently lose entries; a crash mid-write leaves truncated JSON and load_fetch_index then returns default(), mass-invalidating all previously cached fetches.
findings.evidence: mcp/lib.rs:2285-2315 uses std::fs::write (truncate+write) with no lock, no atomic temp+rename, no sync_data; load_fetch_index at :2271-2276 swallows parse errors.
findings.fix: Reuse the recovery crate's atomic_write_json pattern (sibling-tmp + fs4 lock + sync_data + rename + counter-nonce tmp name).

findings.title: MCP session dedup race — README's headline 99.7% repeat-read benchmark does not reproduce
findings.impact: The 'session dedup' feature exists (SessionMemory + unchanged_read_note, on by default) but is not enforced across pipelined requests in the 4-worker pool. README benchmark row '16,712 → 45 (99.7%)' is unreproducible.
findings.evidence: EMPIRICAL: two pipelined `tools/call read` requests on the same MCP session return byte-identical 732-char responses (185 vs 150 visible tokens — observed in this demo). Feature: session.rs:22-92, lib.rs:380-405. Worker pool: stdio.rs:37-44, :93-103. First read does not update session memory until persist completes (lib.rs:446-519). Benchmark harness uses `sleep 1` instead of response-gated send: scripts/benchmark_tokens.sh:52-63.
findings.fix: Serialize same-key reads via an in-flight-serve table keyed by ServeKey; second identical request waits for the first to persist, then emits unchanged note. Fix the benchmark to await response id=2 before sending id=3. Re-run README numbers from the fixed harness.
findings.source: design review #10 (added after my empirical observation)
findings.claim_contradicted: README benchmark row 'Re-read the same file (session dedup): 16,712 → 45 tokens, 99.7%'

findings.title: Command rewriting (-q / --silent) makes 'byte-exact recoverable' untrue for build/test logs
findings.impact: What's cached is the rewritten command's bytes, not the user's original command. Test failures hidden by -q can't be recovered.
findings.evidence: filters/lib.rs:170-172, :300-323 add quiet flags to build/test/package commands by default.
findings.fix: Do not rewrite output semantics by default; if quiet rewriting stays, mark explicitly lossy and exclude from exact-output claims.

findings.title: Rollback manifests can collide within one second
findings.impact: Two applies within the same second share an id/path; the second overwrites the first manifest, destroying the ability to restore the true prior state.
findings.evidence: install/lib.rs:929-931 (id is seconds-only); install/lib.rs:565-569 (writes without uniqueness enforcement).
findings.fix: Nanoseconds + random suffix; OpenOptions::create_new; fail/retry on collision; include apply-transaction id in every verification row.

findings.title: `tz_edit` write race + missing fsync; doc claim overstates crash safety
findings.impact: Two same-PID workers editing the same path interleave bytes in the shared tmp file; no fsync/parent-sync means power loss between rename and data-flush can leave the user's file truncated.
findings.evidence: mcp/render.rs:253-271 — tmp is `.{file}.tz-edit-{pid}` (no per-call nonce), no create_new, no advisory lock; fs::write with no sync_data. Compare recovery/lib.rs:1069+:1248-1259 which uses AtomicUsize+create_new+sync_data.
findings.fix: Add process-wide AtomicUsize counter for tmp suffix; create_new(true); sync_data before rename; best-effort parent-dir sync_all.

findings.title: JSON-RPC error replies emitted for malformed notifications (spec violation)
findings.impact: Server replies with id:null for notifications that fail params/method/jsonrpc validation; strict clients treat unexpected responses as protocol violations.
findings.evidence: mcp/jsonrpc.rs:91-141 — checks at :91, :102, :113, :126 all reply before the notification short-circuit at :139.
findings.fix: Hoist `if !object.contains_key('id') { return None; }` to the top of handle_jsonrpc_request.

findings.title: `ingest --stdin` has no input cap
findings.impact: Malicious or accidental large stdin exhausts memory before capsule/cache limits apply.
findings.evidence: tokenzero/src/main.rs:659-663 uses unbounded read_to_string; cli_args.rs:302-310 exposes no max-input flag.
findings.fix: Default byte cap with streaming/spill path; explicit --max-input-bytes / --allow-large to opt out.

findings.title: Install `atomic_write` is missing parent-directory fsync
findings.impact: Same crash window as #12 for install manifests; power loss after user-observed 'install ok' can leave the file pointing at no entry.
findings.evidence: install/lib.rs:883-911 calls sync_all on data file but never on the parent dir. pulse/src/lib.rs:814 has sync_parent helper — install could mirror it.
findings.fix: After rename, best-effort open the parent dir and sync_all (no-op on Windows).

findings.title: MCP protocol-version docs and implementation disagree
findings.impact: Clients may negotiate versions not documented in the README.
findings.evidence: README.md:268-271 lists 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2026-07-28-RC; mcp/jsonrpc.rs:7-14 also accepts 2024-11-05 and DRAFT-2026-v1.
findings.fix: Align docs and code; document fallback behavior for unsupported versions.
